items.exact_source: For p > 0, the p-th moment of X is defined as E X^p, and the p-th absolute moment is E |X|^p.
items.issue: The chapter's random variables are real-valued, but no negative-base convention or restriction is supplied for X^p when p is a noninteger positive real. A constant X=-1 with p=1/2 already has no real algebraic square-root value. Choosing Mathlib Real.rpow on negative arguments or replacing by absolute powers would silently select semantics not specified in this PDF.
items.authorized_source_research: Complete seven-page source text and rendered formulas inspected; no operative definition or convention resolves negative-base noninteger powers. Pinned Mathlib's negative-base Real.rpow convention was inspected only as a candidate library meaning, not as source authority. External source consultation is explicitly forbidden.
implemented_supported_domains: Signed natural moments, including partial signed-extended expectation and exact infinity-minus-infinity undefinedness
All real positive powers of nonnegative random variables, with extended nonnegative expectations
Absolute moments for every real p>0, including all finite/infinite layercake identities
items.independent_assessment: Source-only and statement reviewers agree the supported domains are legitimate, but do not identify the full printed arbitrary signed/noninteger semantics.
items.required_nonlocal_resolution: A source-authoritative convention/domain correction or explicit operator-authorized semantic amendment; no new proof can determine missing source meaning.

items.handling: Keep 0<p≤q≤∞, retain infinite norms and infinity endpoint.

items.issue: Normalized CLT divides by standard deviation without excluding zero variance; constant iid variables are a counterexample to a standard Gaussian limit.
items.handling: Explicit finite positive variance; all zero-variance-meaningful results (SLLN, finite sample mean rate, variance formulas) retain zero variance.

items.issue: Exercise1.2.2's subtraction is undefined if both tails integrate to infinity.
items.handling: Option EReal marks exactly infinity-minus-infinity as none; every defined extended case retained, plus separate integrable real identity.

Lp Banach/Hilbert use a.e. quotient; real finite expectations and variance use actual integrability/square integrability. Nonnegative extended MGF/moments and explicitly infinite source identities use ENNReal. Jensen includes infinite positive RHS with proved finite negative part. Finite-sum variance is explicitly within the finite-variance domain; no totalized divergent real integral is counted as source coverage.

Triangle inequality for p<1 fails in general, witnessed on fair Bool for every positive p<1; no claim of failure on all probability spaces. CDF convergence at every real point is used for continuous Gaussian limit; Poisson limit uses genuine weak convergence. Rare-event O(1) prose is motivation governed by exact subsequent triangular-array hypotheses.
